key_insight: CREW replaces fixed multi-agent pipelines with reinforcement-learned coordination, letting LLM agents dynamically choose how to collaborate when generating related work sections.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for scalable literature-mining systems because it improves output quality while reducing token cost, making automated scholarly writing more practical.
method: Multi-agent LLM framework for related work generation
Agents autonomously select actions: Retrieve, Disseminate, Compose, Critique
Policy optimized with Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO)
evidence_signal: Experiments on a standard RWG benchmark show substantial quality gains over strong baselines, with significantly lower token cost.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on stable RL training and careful action design, so deployment may be sensitive to reward shaping and agent coordination failures.
paper_title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation
